pr.title: coverage: Clarify some parts of coverage counter creation
pr.description:
This is a series of semi-related changes that are trying to make the `counters` module easier to read, understand, and modify.

For example, the existing code happens to avoid ever using the count for a `TerminatorKind::Yield` node as the count for its sole out-edge (since doing so would be incorrect), but doesn't do so explicitly, so seemingly-innocent changes can result in baffling test failures.

This PR also takes the opportunity to simplify some debug-logging code that was making its surrounding code disproportionately hard to read.

There should be no changes to the resulting coverage instrumentation/mappings, as demonstrated by the absence of changes to the coverage test suite.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: PR #130380 is an explicitly semantics-preserving refactor: it adds `is_out_summable`/`simple_successor`/`sole_predecessor` and splits `CoverageSuccessors::Yield` out of `NotChainable`, while stating (and demonstrating by an unchanged coverage test suite) that emitted coverage counters/mappings do not change. In the pre-PR code, a Yield BCB's single successor was already excluded from edge-counter creation by the `successors.len() > 1` guard, and a single-predecessor resume node received a physical node counter directly, so the "wrong" reuse of the Yield node count for its resume edge never actually occurred. The denied transformation is a hypothetical latent hazard ("seemingly-innocent changes" could cause it), not a historical incorrect rewrite with a concretely different result. Constructing a pair that models a guard-dropping variant would manufacture a difference not present in the historical patch. Hence no source-grounded original/transformed pair with genuinely differing defined executions can be validated.

analysis.originalLogic: Pre-PR `counters.rs` decided node-vs-edge counters using `bcb_has_multiple_in_edges(to_bcb)`, then a source shortcut `if self.bcb_successors(from_bcb).len() == 1 { return self.get_or_make_node_counter(from_bcb); }`. It handled `TerminatorKind::Yield` by mapping it to `CoverageSuccessors::NotChainable(std::slice::from_ref(resume))`, which gives the Yield block one successor without marking whether the node count may be reused for that out-edge. The PR states this only implicitly avoided the wrong reuse: the old code "happens to avoid ever using the count for a `TerminatorKind::Yield` node as the count for its sole out-edge".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Applying the single-out-edge counter-elision shortcut to a BCB ending in `TerminatorKind::Yield`, i.e. reusing the Yield node's counter as the counter for its sole resume out-edge. The PR makes this impossible by adding `is_out_summable` and requiring it in `simple_successor`; it notes the old code avoided this only implicitly, so this is a latent hazard guarded by refactoring, not a reproduced bug or output change.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR under coverage instrumentation for coroutines/generators (including async lowering) containing `TerminatorKind::Yield`, where the Yield block has exactly one coverage-relevant out-edge to its resume block and the BCB graph is being assigned counters.
analysis.summary: Refactor of coverage counter creation that makes an existing correctness invariant explicit: a BCB ending in `TerminatorKind::Yield` is not "out summable", so its node count must not be reused as the count of its single resume out-edge. The PR also replaces `bcb_has_multiple_in_edges`/successor-count shortcuts with `sole_predecessor` and `simple_successor`. It reports no changes to coverage instrumentation/mappings and no coverage test-suite changes.
analysis.trigger: `MakeBcbCounters` processes an edge `from_bcb -> to_bcb` where `from_bcb` ends in `TerminatorKind::Yield` and has exactly one successor, and tries to avoid creating an edge counter by reusing the source node's counter.
preconditions: The MIR contains a coroutine/generator or async body with a `TerminatorKind::Yield` terminator.
The Yield block ends its BCB (Yield is not chainable) and has exactly one coverage-relevant out-edge (the resume edge).
Counter assignment is deciding whether an out-edge can reuse the source node's counter or needs its own edge counter.
pitfalls: A yield terminator has exactly one successor but must not be chained, because its resume edge has a different execution count.
`is_out_summable` must be false for a node ending in `TerminatorKind::Yield`, because the yielding coroutine might not be resumed.
Never use a single-successor shortcut alone to reuse a node counter; `simple_successor` requires both exactly one successor and `is_out_summable`.
When the target has a sole predecessor, `edge_has_no_counter` must consult the target node's counter rather than the edge map, since the edge normally has no separate counter.
START_BCB has no in-edges, so summing predecessors is invalid; nodes with one predecessor or a self-predecessor must get a physical node counter to avoid infinite recursion.
Do not conflate this out-summability issue with borrowing/overwrite effects; the invariant concerns execution counts of Yield resume edges.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused coverage tests for generator/coroutine and async bodies containing `Yield`, and compare emitted counter mappings to ensure the resume edge gets the correct counter/expression rather than the Yield node's count. At unit level, assert `CoverageSuccessors::Yield(..).is_out_summable() == false` and that `simple_successor` returns `None` for a Yield block with one successor, while it returns the successor for an out-summable single-successor block. Exercise START_BCB and self-loop predecessor cases to confirm physical node counters are used. No compiler was built and no execution/reproduction is claimed here.
evidence: the existing code happens to avoid ever using the count for a `TerminatorKind::Yield` node as the count for its sole out-edge (since doing so would be incorrect), but doesn't do so explicitly, so seemingly-innocent changes can result in baffling test failures.
There should be no changes to the resulting coverage instrumentation/mappings, as demonstrated by the absence of changes to the coverage test suite.
